info.title: apollo-rest-api
info.summary: Programmatic access to Apollo's sales intelligence and engagement platform — data enrichment, prospect and company search, and go-to-market workflow management.
info.description:
The Apollo API provides programmatic access to [Apollo](https://www.apollo.io/), the all-in-one sales intelligence and engagement platform. Use it to enrich people and company data (individually or in bulk), search Apollo's database of over 240 million contacts and 30 million companies, and manage accounts, contacts, deals, sequences, tasks, calls, and conversations in your go-to-market workflows.

## Base URL

All API requests are made to `https://api.apollo.io/api/v1`.

## Authentication

- **Apollo users** authenticate with an API key passed in the `x-api-key` request header. See [Create API Keys](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key).
- **Apollo partners** building integrations on behalf of mutual users authenticate with the [OAuth 2.0 authorization flow](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/use-oauth-20-authorization-flow-to-access-apollo-user-information-partners).

## Rate limits & credits

Rate limits and credit consumption depend on your [Apollo pricing plan](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/api-pricing). Check your current limits and usage with the [view API usage stats and rate limits](https://docs.apollo.io/reference/view-api-usage-stats) endpoint. For more details, see [Rate Limits](https://docs.apollo.io/reference/rate-limits) and the [API FAQs](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/apollo-api-faqs).

New to the API? Start with the [Apollo API overview](https://docs.apollo.io/reference/apollo-api).

post.description:
Endpoint essentials
API key access api/v1/people/match or Master API key
OAuth scopes people_match
Free account access Requires an Apollo account registered with a work email address. Additional account eligibility requirements may apply. Paid accounts aren't affected.
Credit usage 1–9 credits per person without waterfall enrichment
Credits are charged only if credit-consuming data is found: 1 credit for demographics or email, plus 8 credits if a mobile phone is returned. If no credit-consuming data is found, the request consumes 0 credits. Demographic credit usage depends on `match_confidence`. Apollo doesn't charge a demographic credit when `match_confidence` is `none`. When `match_confidence` is `low`, Apollo charges a demographic credit only if it returns data you didn't send. Email and mobile phone credit usage isn't determined by `match_confidence`. Learn more about API pricing and credits.

If waterfall enrichment is used for phone or email, credit usage depends on the returned data and the vendors included in your waterfall enrichment configuration; some vendors consume credits per lookup even when no data is found.
Enrichment is when you refresh existing records so your prospecting data is up-to-date.

Use the people enrichment endpoint to enrich data for one person. To enrich data for up to ten people with a single API call, use the bulk people enrichment endpoint instead.

Apollo relies on the information you pass via the endpoint's parameters to identify the correct person to enrich. If you provide more information about a person, Apollo is more likely to find a match within its database. If you only provide general information, such as a name without a domain or email address, you might receive a `200` response, but the response indicates that no records have been enriched. Check `match_confidence` in the response to understand how confidently Apollo matched the submitted information: - `high`: Apollo found a high-confidence match for the submitted person information. - `medium`: Apollo identified a likely match with medium confidence. - `low`: Apollo identified a possible match with low confidence. - `none`: Apollo couldn't find a match for the submitted person information. By default, this endpoint doesn't return personal emails or phone numbers. Use the `reveal_personal_emails` and `reveal_phone_number` parameters to retrieve emails and phone numbers. When you use `reveal_phone_number`, provide a valid `webhook_url` so Apollo can deliver completed phone enrichment results. Alternatively, set `poll_only=true` and [poll webhook results](ref:poll-webhook-result) with the top-level `request_id_str`. Poll only when `phone_enrichment.status` is `pending`. Do not use `phone_enrichment.request_id`. If the status is `skipped` or `not_attempted`, Apollo did not create a phone enrichment job and polling returns `404 request_id_unknown`. Webhook requirements: - **HTTPS Required:** Your endpoint must be publicly accessible over HTTPS. - **Rate Limiting:** Ensure your webhook endpoint can handle the volume of webhook traffic sent by Apollo. - **Idempotency:** Apollo may retry webhook calls; your endpoint should be idempotent to handle duplicate payloads safely. Apollo returns the main enrichment response synchronously, then sends the requested phone numbers to the [webhook asynchronously](doc:retrieve-mobile-phone-numbers-for-contacts#webhook-response) or makes them available to poll, depending on your request. For a pending phone enrichment request, [poll webhook results](ref:poll-webhook-result) with the top-level `request_id_str` from the people enrichment response. You can also use the `run_waterfall_email` and `run_waterfall_phone` parameters to run waterfall enrichment. [Waterfall enrichment](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/34071089002509-Waterfall-Enrichment-Overview) gives you broader data coverage by checking connected third-party data sources for contact emails and phone numbers. When your request includes a waterfall parameter, provide a valid `webhook_url`. Alternatively, set `poll_only=true` and [poll webhook result](ref:poll-webhook-result) with the top-level `request_id_str` returned by the response. Passing `poll_only=true` together with `webhook_url` returns a `400` error (`WEBHOOK_URL_WITH_POLL_ONLY`). Apollo then returns an immediate synchronous response with demographic and firmographic data, along with a waterfall enrichment request status. Apollo delivers enriched emails or phone numbers asynchronously to the [configured webhook](doc:enrich-phone-and-email-using-data-waterfall#asynchronous-webhook-response-1) or makes them available to poll, depending on your request.

parameters.name: run_waterfall_phone

parameters.name: reveal_personal_emails
parameters.description:
Set to `true` if you want to enrich the person's data with personal emails. This potentially consumes credits as part of your Apollo pricing plan. The default value is `false`.

If a person resides in a GDPR-compliant region, Apollo will not reveal their personal email.

parameters.name: reveal_phone_number
parameters.description:
Set to `true` if you want to enrich the person's data with all available phone numbers, including mobile phone numbers. This potentially consumes credits as part of your Apollo pricing plan. The default value is `false`.

To receive completed phone enrichment results, provide a webhook URL with the `webhook_url` parameter. Alternatively, set `poll_only=true` and omit `webhook_url` to retrieve the result by polling.

parameters.name: webhook_url
parameters.description:
Provide this parameter to receive phone or waterfall enrichment results by webhook. Your webhook URL must be publicly accessible over HTTPS.

When `poll_only=true`, omit `webhook_url` and retrieve the result by polling instead.

If phone numbers are not delivered to the webhook URL, try applying UTF-8 encoding to the webhook URL.

Example: `https://webhook.site/11f2643a-b1b4-c6be-8e6a-6c7da2c12610`; `https%3A%2F%2Fwebhook.site%2F11f2643a-b1b4-c6be-8e6a-6c7da2c12610`

parameters.name: poll_only
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to receive phone or waterfall enrichment results by polling instead of a webhook. When `poll_only` is `true`, omit `webhook_url` — Apollo returns a `request_id` you can pass to the poll webhook result endpoint to retrieve the result.

Passing `poll_only=true` together with `webhook_url` returns a `400` error (`WEBHOOK_URL_WITH_POLL_ONLY`). The default value is `false`.

phone_enrichment.message: Phone enrichment is processing asynchronously. Retrieve the result by polling GET /api/v1/webhook_result/{request_id} with the top-level `request_id_str` field from this response. Retry after ~10 seconds.

Waterfall enrichment result.summary: Response when run_waterfall_email or run_waterfall_phone is true

waterfall.message: Waterfall enrichment request accepted. Results will be sent to the provided webhook URL.

request_id.description: The signed 64-bit request ID for the enrichment request.

request_id_str.description: The exact string representation of the top-level request ID. When `phone_enrichment.status` is `pending`, pass this value unchanged to `GET /api/v1/webhook_result/{request_id}`. Do not pass `phone_enrichment.request_id`.

status.description:
`success` for any `200` response. Error responses return `failed` instead.

This reflects the enrichment call itself, not whether any person was matched — a request that matches nobody still returns `success`.

error_code.description: Always `null` on a `200` response. Populated only on error responses.

error_message.description: Always `null` on a `200` response. Populated only on error responses.

total_requested_enrichments.description: The number of objects you sent in the `details[]` array. Always returned.

unique_enriched_records.description:
The number of distinct people that consumed credits on this request.

This is a billing count, not a match count. A person who was matched but returned no credit-consuming data isn't included, so this can be lower than the number of entries in `matches` — or `0` while `matches` is non-empty. Duplicate entries in `details[]` that resolve to the same person are counted once.

**Not returned** when `run_waterfall_email` or `run_waterfall_phone` is `true`; those requests return the `waterfall` object instead.

missing_records.description:
The number of entries in `details[]` that Apollo couldn't match to a person in its database.

**Not returned** when `run_waterfall_email` or `run_waterfall_phone` is `true`; those requests return the `waterfall` object instead.

credits_consumed.description:
The total credits this request consumed.

This can be a fraction rather than a whole number, depending on your plan's credit pricing, so parse it as a decimal rather than an integer.

**Not returned** when `run_waterfall_email` or `run_waterfall_phone` is `true`; those requests return the `waterfall` object instead. Waterfall credit usage is reported separately, since enrichment completes asynchronously.

waterfall.description:
Returned **only** when you set `run_waterfall_email` or `run_waterfall_phone` to `true`. It reports whether Apollo accepted the waterfall request, whose results arrive asynchronously at your `webhook_url`.

When this object is present, `unique_enriched_records`, `missing_records`, and `credits_consumed` are omitted from the response.

status.description: Whether the waterfall enrichment request was accepted for asynchronous processing. A `200` response with a non-accepted status means no webhook will be delivered — read `message` for the reason.

message.example: Waterfall enrichment request accepted. Results will be sent to the provided webhook URL.
message.description: A human-readable explanation of the waterfall status. When a request isn't accepted, this states why — for example, that no waterfall enrichment template is configured for your team.

unprocessed_attributes.description: Present only when some of the records you submitted couldn't be queued for waterfall enrichment. Each entry echoes the attributes Apollo was unable to process.

phone_enrichment.description:
Returned when you set `reveal_phone_number` to `true`, at least one person in `details[]` was matched, and you aren't using `run_waterfall_phone`. Phone numbers are enriched asynchronously and delivered to your `webhook_url` or made available to poll when `poll_only=true`.

## Endpoint essentials **API key access:** `api/v1/mixed_people/api_search` or `Master API key` **OAuth scopes:** `mixed_people_api_search` **Free account access:** Requires an Apollo account registered with a work email address. Additional account eligibility requirements may apply. Paid accounts aren't affected. **Credit usage:** `0 credits` — [Learn more about API pricing and credits](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/api-pricing). People are net-new prospects you haven't yet saved as contacts on Apollo.

Use the people API search endpoint to find new prospects. Several filters are available to help narrow your search. This endpoint doesn't return email addresses or phone numbers. Use the people enrichment or bulk people enrichment endpoints to enrich data.

To protect Apollo's performance for all users, this endpoint has a display limit of 50,000 records (100 records per page, up to 500 pages). Add more filters to narrow your search results as much as possible.

parameters.name: person_titles[]
parameters.description:
Job titles held by the people you want to find. For a person to be included in search results, they only need to match 1 of the job titles you add. Adding more job titles expands your search results.

Results also include job titles with the same terms, even if they are not exact matches. For example, searching for `marketing manager` might return people with the job title `content marketing manager`.

Use this parameter in combination with the `person_seniorities[]` parameter to find people based on specific job functions and seniority levels.

Examples: `sales development representative`; `marketing manager`; `research analyst`

parameters.name: include_similar_titles
parameters.description:
This parameter determines whether people with job titles similar to the titles you define in the `person_titles[]` parameter are returned in the response.

Set this parameter to `false` when using `person_titles[]` to return only strict matches for job titles.

parameters.name: person_not_titles[]
parameters.description:
Exclude people whose current job title matches any of these job titles. This is the counterpart to `person_titles[]`.

Like `person_titles[]`, matching isn't limited to exact job titles. For example, excluding `intern` also excludes people with the job title `sales intern`.

The combined number of unique job titles in `person_titles[]` and `person_not_titles[]` must be less than 100. Requests that exceed this limit return a `422` error.

Examples: `intern`; `assistant`

parameters.name: person_not_past_titles[]
parameters.description:
Exclude people who held any of these job titles in a previous role. Only past roles are checked; a person's current job title isn't affected by this filter. To exclude current job titles, use `person_not_titles[]`.

You can add fewer than 100 unique job titles. Requests that exceed this limit return a `422` error.

Examples: `intern`; `recruiter`

parameters.name: q_keywords
parameters.description: A string of words over which we want to filter the results.

parameters.name: q_person_name
parameters.description:
The name of the person you want to find. Use this parameter to search by name only, independent of any other filters. Search results include people whose name contains all the words you enter.

Examples: `Jon Snow`; `Maria`

parameters.name: person_locations[]
parameters.description:
The location where people live. You can search across cities, US states, countries, and postal codes (ZIP codes). Postal codes are supported for the United States, Germany, and the United Kingdom. To filter by a US ZIP code or a UK postcode, pass it on its own, such as `94105`. For a German postal code, add the country, such as `10115, germany`, because a five-digit code on its own can match a US ZIP code instead.

To find people based on the headquarters locations of their current employer, use the `organization_locations` parameter.

Examples: `california`; `ireland`; `chicago`; `94105`; `10115, germany`

parameters.name: person_not_locations[]
parameters.description:
Exclude people from your search results based on where they live. You can use cities, US states, countries, and postal codes (ZIP codes) as locations to exclude. Postal codes are supported for the United States, Germany, and the United Kingdom. For a German postal code, add the country, such as `10115, germany`, because a five-digit code on its own can match a US ZIP code instead.

This is the counterpart to `person_locations[]`. To exclude people based on the headquarters location of their current employer, use the `organization_not_locations[]` parameter.

Examples: `texas`; `ireland`; `94105`

parameters.name: person_seniorities[]
parameters.description:
The job seniority that people hold within their current employer. This enables you to find people that currently hold positions at certain reporting levels, such as Director level or senior IC level.

For a person to be included in search results, they only need to match 1 of the seniorities you add. Adding more seniorities expands your search results.

Searches only return results based on their current job title, so searching for Director-level employees only returns people that currently hold a Director-level title. If someone was previously a Director, but is currently a VP, they would not be included in your search results.

Use this parameter in combination with the `person_titles[]` parameter to find people based on specific job functions and seniority levels.

The following options can be used for this parameter:
  • owner
  • founder
  • c_suite
  • partner
  • vp
  • head
  • director
  • manager
  • senior
  • entry
  • intern

parameters.name: organization_locations[]
parameters.description:
The location of the company headquarters for a person's current employer. You can search across cities, US states, countries, and postal codes (ZIP codes). Postal codes are supported for the United States, Germany, and the United Kingdom. To filter by a US ZIP code or a UK postcode, pass it on its own, such as `10017`. For a German postal code, add the country, such as `10115, germany`, because a five-digit code on its own can match a US ZIP code instead.

If a company has several office locations, results are still based on the headquarters location. For example, if you search `chicago` but a company's HQ location is in `boston`, people that work for the Boston-based company won't appear in your results, even if they match other parameters.

To find people based on their personal location, use the `person_locations` parameter.

Examples: `texas`; `tokyo`; `spain`; `10017`; `10115, germany`

parameters.name: organization_not_locations[]
parameters.description:
Exclude people from your search results based on the headquarters location of their current employer. You can use cities, US states, countries, and postal codes (ZIP codes) as locations to exclude. Postal codes are supported for the United States, Germany, and the United Kingdom. For a German postal code, add the country, such as `10115, germany`, because a five-digit code on its own can match a US ZIP code instead.

This is the counterpart to `organization_locations[]`. To exclude people based on where they live, use the `person_not_locations[]` parameter.

Examples: `minnesota`; `ireland`; `10017`

parameters.name: organization_industry_tag_ids[]
parameters.description:
The Apollo IDs for the industries of the person's current employer. For a person to be included in search results, their employer only needs to match one of the industries you add.

Each industry in the Apollo database has a unique ID. To find industry IDs, call the organization enrichment endpoint for a company in the industry you want. The `industry_tag_id` field contains the ID of the company's primary industry, and the `industry_tag_hash` field maps each of the company's industry names to its ID.

To search by industry name instead of ID, use the `organization_industries[]` parameter.

Example: `5567cd4773696439b10b0000`

parameters.name: organization_not_industry_tag_ids[]
parameters.description:
Exclude people whose current employer belongs to any of these industries, identified by Apollo industry ID. This is the counterpart to `organization_industry_tag_ids[]`.

To find industry IDs, refer to the `organization_industry_tag_ids[]` parameter.

Example: `5567cd4773696439b10b0000`

parameters.name: organization_industries[]
parameters.description:
The industry names for the person's current employer. For a person to be included in search results, their employer only needs to match one of the industries you add.

Values must exactly match an Apollo industry name, including capitalization and punctuation. Apollo industry names are lowercase. Use the values that Apollo returns in the `industries` field of the organization enrichment endpoint. Partial matches aren't supported.

To search by Apollo industry ID instead, use the `organization_industry_tag_ids[]` parameter.

Examples: `information technology & services`; `hospital & health care`

parameters.name: organization_naics_codes[]
parameters.description:
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes for the person's current employer. For a person to be included in search results, their employer only needs to match one of the codes you add.

Codes match by prefix, so a shorter code matches every code that starts with it. For example, `5415` matches `541511` and `541512`. You can also enter a range of codes separated by a hyphen. For example, `31-33` matches all codes that start with `31`, `32`, or `33`.

Examples: `541511`; `5415`; `31-33`

parameters.name: organization_headcount_growth_range[min]
parameters.description:

Enter the percentage as a whole number, without a percent sign or decimal point: use `10` for 10% growth. This is a lower bound, so sending a minimum on its own returns every match at or above that figure. Negative values are accepted, but `-20` alone still includes flat and growing employers, because everything above -20% also matches. To isolate employers that shrank, pair a negative minimum with a negative maximum, such as a minimum of `-20` and a maximum of `-1`.

Use `organization_headcount_growth_range[max]` to set the upper bound of the range. You must also send `organization_headcount_growth_past_n_months`.

Examples: `10`; `50`

## Endpoint essentials **API key access:** `api/v1/mixed_companies/search` or `Master API key` **OAuth scopes:** `mixed_companies_search` **Free account access:** Requires an Apollo account registered with a work email address. Additional account eligibility requirements may apply. Paid accounts aren't affected. **Credit usage:** `1 credit per page` This endpoint consumes 1 Apollo credit per page, with up to 100 results per page. Learn more about [API pricing and credits](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/api-pricing). Organizations are companies you haven't yet saved as accounts on Apollo.

Use the organization search endpoint to find companies in the Apollo database. Several filters are available to help narrow your search.

To protect Apollo's performance for all users, this endpoint has a display limit of 50,000 records (100 records per page, up to 500 pages). Add more filters to narrow your search results as much as possible.

Each range you add needs to be a string, with the upper and lower numbers of the range separated only by a comma.

Examples: `1,10`; `250,500`; `10000,20000`

parameters.name: organization_locations[]
parameters.description:
The location of the company headquarters. You can search across cities, US states, countries, and postal codes (ZIP codes). Postal codes are supported for the United States, Germany, and the United Kingdom. To filter by a US ZIP code or a UK postcode, pass it on its own, such as `10017`. For a German postal code, add the country, such as `10115, germany`, because a five-digit code on its own can match a US ZIP code instead.

If a company has several office locations, results are still based on the headquarters location. For example, if you search `chicago` but a company's HQ location is in `boston`, any Boston-based companies won't appearch in your search results, even if they match other parameters..

To exclude companies based on location, use the `organization_not_locations` parameter.

Examples: `texas`; `tokyo`; `spain`; `10017`; `10115, germany`

parameters.name: organization_not_locations[]
parameters.description:
Exclude companies from search results based on the location of the company headquarters. You can use cities, US states, countries, and postal codes (ZIP codes) as locations to exclude. Postal codes are supported for the United States, Germany, and the United Kingdom. For a German postal code, add the country, such as `10115, germany`, because a five-digit code on its own can match a US ZIP code instead.

This parameter is useful for ensuring you do not prospect in an undesirable territory. For example, if you use `ireland` as a value, no Ireland-based companies appear in your search results.

Examples: `minnesota`; `ireland`; `seoul`

parameters.name: organization_industry_tag_ids[]

The `industry_tag_id` field contains the ID of the company's primary industry, and the `industry_tag_hash` field maps each of the company's industry names to its ID.

To search by industry name instead of ID, use the `organization_industries[]` parameter.

Example: `5567cd4773696439b10b0000`

Example: `5567cd4773696439b10b0000`

## Endpoint essentials **API key access:** `api/v1/users/api_profile` or `Master API key` **OAuth scopes:** `read_user_profile` **Credit usage:** `0 credits` — [Learn more about API pricing and credits](https://docs.apollo.io/docs/api-pricing). **Authentication note:** Default scope — granted automatically on every OAuth token. Users are the people who use your Apollo workspace.

Use the get current user profile endpoint to retrieve the authenticated profile of the person who owns the API key being used.

By default, the endpoint returns the user's identity fields. Set the `include_credit_usage` query parameter to `true` to also return the user's and team's credit usage and remaining credit balances.

If you call this endpoint without valid access credentials, you receive a `401` response.

parameters.name: include_credit_usage
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to include credit usage and remaining credit details (lead, direct dial, export, AI, and power-up credits) in the response. Accepts boolean (`true`/`false`) or string (`"true"`/`"false"`) values. Defaults to `false`.

Example: `true`

num_credits_remaining.description: Remaining lead credits for the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

effective_num_lead_credits.description: Effective lead credit allowance for the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

num_lead_credits_used.description: Lead credits used by the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

effective_num_direct_dial_credits.description: Effective direct dial credit allowance for the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

num_direct_dial_credits_used.description: Direct dial credits used by the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

effective_num_export_credits.description: Effective export credit allowance for the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

num_export_credits_used.description: Export credits used by the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

effective_num_ai_credits.description: Effective AI credit allowance for the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

num_ai_credits_used.description: AI credits used by the user. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

effective_num_power_up_credits.description: Effective power-up credit allowance for the team. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

num_power_up_credits_used.description: Power-up credits used (user this cycle on unified credits, otherwise team total). Only present when `include_credit_usage=true`.

total_unified_credits_used.description: Sum of lead, direct dial, export, and power-up credits used. Only present when `include_credit_usage=true` and the team is on unified credits.
